source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:22 ('ויהי בשכן — Or Torah: in one respect this is ONE verse, in the other TWO verses, and so some of its words carry TWO accents each — as one verse: Reuben in revia, and-he-lay in pashta, Bilhah in pashta, his-father in zaqef qatan, Israel in etnachta; as two: Reuben in zaqef qatan, and-he-lay in zaqef gadol, Bilhah in tipcha, his-father in etnachta, Israel closing the verse — the way of the Ten Commandments')
claim_en: THE REUBEN VERSE, COMMITTED TO ONE: the tradition carries 35:22 doubly — one verse in one reading, TWO verses in the other, some words bearing two accents at once as in the Ten Commandments (Or Torah's two full lists quoted by Minchat Shai). SNAPSHOT's stream stores it as ONE verse with a single accent per word — the twelve-sons clause continuing unbroken after 'and Israel heard' — and the accents follow the one-verse cantillation at every station except ראובן itself, which carries the TWO-verse reading's zaqef qatan (DB-checked): the doubled tradition flattened to one line, with Reuben's own word keeping the other reading's mark.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:18 ('בנימין — FULL per the Masorah, and per Sotah, the chapter of the stones: the son of the RIGHT hand, written with its yod')
claim_en: BENJAMIN BORN FULL: at the naming — Rachel's בן־אוני answered by his father's בנימין (35:18) — the name is written FULL with its yod exactly as the Masorah and the Talmud's Sotah discussion rule; and the fullness maps the name's whole career: all SEVEN full tokens stand in Genesis, where Benjamin lives and is wept over, while every bare token of the tribal rosters of Numbers runs lean (builder-checked): the living son full, the census-name lean.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:5 ('סביבותיהם — in ALL our books and the Hilleli FULL-OF-FULL, vav and two yods; so the handwritten Masorah (two full-of-full, the terror-verse and Judges 2:12) and so the Ramah explicitly; the Yerushalmi lean')
claim_en: THE TERROR-VERSE'S LEVELED SURROUNDINGS: at 'the TERROR of God was on the cities AROUND THEM' (35:5) Minchat Shai's whole chain — all his books, the Hilleli, the written Masorah, the Ramah — rules the word full-of-full with its vav; SNAPSHOT writes it LEAN, level with the two lean members at Korach's swallowing (Num 16:34) and the pasture-cities (Num 35:2, all three DB-checked): the stream joining the Yerushalmi's lean camp alone against the entire ruling chain — a front-rank spelling discrepancy, filed.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:2 ('הסרו — lean of yod in all the books and the Hilleli; the Masorah pairs it with its full partner in Jeremiah — REMOVE the foreskin of your heart; so the Ramah and Minchat Kohen')
claim_en: PUT-AWAY, ONCE AND LEAN: הסרו ('PUT AWAY the foreign gods in your midst,' 35:2 — the purge before Bethel) — the word's only Torah token, written lean of its yod as the whole chain rules; its one Scripture partner is written full in Jeremiah's 'REMOVE the foreskin of your heart' (4:4, named): the idols put away lean, the heart full.
middah: ink (the written form — the Masorah's note)

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:16 ('לבוא — full in all the books against the Yerushalmi and one old variant; not counted among the Masorah's lean members; so the Ramah') + 35:17 ('בהקשתה — lean, the Masorah marking NONE LIKE IT; the Hilleli and the Ramah explicit, against the Yerushalmi')
claim_en: THE BIRTH-ROAD PAIR: on the road to Ephrath the coming-word לבוא is written FULL as all the books rule (35:16, builder-checked), and the labor-word בהקשתה ('in her HARD labor,' 35:17) is written LEAN — the Masorah's none-like-it, Hilleli and the Ramah against the Yerushalmi: the road whole, the travail one letter short.

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:2 ('בתככם — the kaf with sheva alone, as our custom') + 35:18 ('ויהי — with TWO geresh strokes') + 35:27 ('אשר גר שם — the gimel with the stress-stroke, as in the precise manuscripts')
claim_en: STROKES AND POINTS AS RULED: בתככם ('the foreign gods IN YOUR MIDST,' 35:2) — the kaf with plain sheva as our custom rules; ויהי of the soul's departing (35:18) under gershayim (the double stroke); and גר of 'where Abraham and Isaac SOJOURNED' (35:27) carrying the precise manuscripts' meteg — all three in the stream exactly as ruled (builder-checked).

source: Minchat Shai on Gen 35:7 ('כי שם נגלו אליו האלהים — the Targums render it the ANGELS of God, and so many commentators — profane; but Rashi rules it HOLY, and so the Sanhedrin passage proves, among the verses the heretics seized whose answer stands beside them')
claim_en: THE REVEALED NAME AT BETHEL (classification layer, uninstrumented): 'for there האלהים WERE REVEALED to him' (35:7 — the plural verb over the Name) — the Targums and many read it profane (the angels); Rashi rules it holy, with the Sanhedrin discussion of verses the heretics seized: the classification layer's twelfth station, filed unsettled; SNAPSHOT carries the plural verb the whole dispute turns on.

claim_en: THE VOW AUDIT OPENED AT GEN_48 IS EXECUTED HERE, AND THE COMMAND IS ITS WRIT. The delay penalty recorded at 28:20 - scrutiny follows vows, and delay triggers an audit of the whole ledger - lands as this block's opening command to arise and go up. The chain stacks the enforcement: better a muzzle than an unkept resolve; the hand adjacent to the mouth; in trouble a vow, in relief swept away; and the closing sentence, fulfil, or YOU ARE LIKE ESAU, who vows and does not fulfil. A penalty recorded in one block and executed in another as a narrative command.

check.note: A delay penalty recorded at an earlier block executed here as the narrative's own command, with the full enforcement stack.

claim_en: THE CHAIN FINDS A DEATH THE TORAH NEVER NARRATES, HIDDEN IN A PLACE-NAME. Reading the tree's name as containing a foreign word for OTHER, it concludes that while he sat mourning the nurse, the news of Rebecca's death arrived - a second weeping concealed inside the name, and the only notice the corpus gives of a matriarch's death. The appearing-and-blessing of the next verse is then read as the mourners' blessing. Onkelos renders the name plainly as a plain of weeping, leaving the concealment concealed: one member finds the hidden death, the other declines to.

check.note: An unnarrated death located inside a place-name by a foreign-word reading, with the translation leaving it hidden.

middah: plain (a matriarch's death found in the place-name's foreign word)

claim_en: THE CURSE CHAIN OPENED AT GEN_53 CLOSES AT THIS VERSE. She took the images at 31:19; the curse was pronounced in ignorance at 31:32 - with whomever you find your gods, he shall not live; and she dies here at 35:19. The chain states the sequence explicitly and compares it to an error that issues from a ruler. The rival explanation, that she spoke before her elder sister, and the burial-price account from gen_51 both stand beside it: three causes for one death, all preserved, and this one traceable verse by verse across three blocks.

check.note: A three-verse causal chain across three blocks completing here, with two rival explanations preserved.

claim_en: AN ANTI-MONUMENT MAXIM IS RECORDED AT THE TORAH'S MOST FAMOUS MONUMENT. The received rule that surplus burial funds build the grave-structure is set against Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel: ONE DOES NOT BUILD MONUMENTS FOR THE RIGHTEOUS - THEIR WORDS ARE THEIR MEMORIAL - and the dispute is left standing at the very verse that records a pillar being set up. And the siting is explained as infrastructure: he buried her on the road because he foresaw the exiles passing that way, so that she would plead for them.

claim_en: VERSES ARE WIELDED AS CONSTITUTIONAL INSTRUMENTS, AND THE CHAIN RECORDS IT TWICE. The blessing's terms are parsed into named descendants, and then the striking observation: is it possible that Avner was righteous and yet disputed the kingdom? HE EXPOUNDED - and crowned a rival king ON THIS VERSE. A second pair follows, one verse read to ostracize a tribe and another read to welcome them back. The chain is recording the claim-power of an interpretation, not only its content.

Yochanan extends it FROM THIS VERSE to ALL GARMENTS - the change-your-garments order taken as the source for a broader category. A narrative instruction functioning as the source-text that widens an existing statute's scope.

claim_en: A LINEAGE-CONSERVATION RULE IS STATED AT THE MOMENT THE COUNT COULD HAVE DROPPED. After the offence the verse insists the sons were TWELVE, and the chain reads that as a rule: uprooting a name from the lineage is grave before God. The birthright is then SPLIT rather than transferred - the property share to one son, the genealogical share retained by the offender, reckoned to him even at the hour of corruption. And a table of firsts is built around him, closing with his being first to repent.

check.note: A conservation rule for lineage counts stated where a name could have been struck, with the birthright split rather than transferred.

claim_en: THE ANGEL'S DEFERRAL AT GEN_55 IS HONOURED BY THE TEXT HERE. At 32:30 the wrestler withheld the renaming and said He will reveal Himself to you at Bethel and change your name, and I WILL BE STANDING THERE. At 35:10 the text performs it - no more Jacob, but Israel. A promise made by a character in one block and kept by the narration in another, both inside this derivation group. The chain separately notes the asymmetry with an earlier renaming, where the old name was banned: here it is not, and both names continue.

claim_en: THE CHAIN MARKS A TWO-LANGUAGE SEAM INSIDE ONE NAMING, AND POINTS AT THE TRANSLATION'S OWN COLUMN. Her name for the child is said to be IN ARAMAIC and the father's IN THE SACRED TONGUE - and Onkelos, being the Aramaic member of this declared reading, renders her name in exactly that language. The chain is describing a bilingual seam in the verse while the other member of the shelf occupies one side of it. The third seat of the two-tongues theme in this sweep, after the monument's two names and the honour paid to the language at gen_54.

claim_en: THE VOW'S WHOLE ARC IS CLOSED IN THE TRANSLATION'S OWN BOOKKEEPING. At 28:15 the promise was rendered MY WORD IS YOUR SUPPORT; at 31:3 the recall used the same words; and here the discharge does too - who ACCEPTED MY PRAYER in the day of my distress, and whose WORD WAS MY SUPPORT on the way. Promise, recall and discharge in one vocabulary across three blocks, so the translation keeps the account closed in a way the received text does not.

claim_en: THE CANON'S TRANSPARENCY ABOUT ITS OWN FIGURES IS EXHIBITED AT THIS VERSE. Challenged that a young man could not have withstood temptation at seventeen, the chain answers by OPENING THE BOOK - reading out this chapter's offence and another from a later one - and arguing: the verse did not cover THEM; this one all the more. The argument depends on the corpus recording its own protagonists' failures, and this verse is the exhibit.
